article_title: Students' Epistemological Beliefs and their Chatbot Preferences in AI-mediated Physics Learning
citation: Amogh Sirnoorkar and Omkar Mamidpalliwar. (2026). Students' Epistemological Beliefs and their Chatbot Preferences in AI-mediated Physics Learning. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29385
title: EBAPS five-dimension framework of epistemological beliefs in physical sciences
description: The Epistemological Beliefs Assessment for Physical Sciences is a 30-item questionnaire of Likert-style and multiple-choice items, each scored from 0 (least sophisticated) to 4 (most sophisticated). "The questionnaire probes students' beliefs across the following five non-orthogonal dimensions": structure of scientific knowledge (10 items), nature of knowing and learning (8), real-life applicability (4), evolving knowledge (3), and source of ability to learn (5). The study uses weighted percentage scores per axis to compare belief sophistication across chatbot preference groups.
requirements: Scored via the prescribed rubric with weighted axis scores computed as item sums divided by maximum possible axis score
constraints: The survey authors argue against Cronbach's alpha for this instrument because "students were allowed to disagree with themselves within a subscale" and beliefs may be context-dependent; the study's alpha values were moderate to low (0.13–0.64)
target_learning_goals: epistemological beliefs about the structure, knowing, applicability, evolution, and learnability of scientific knowledge
examples: Administered via Qualtrics a week before the chatbot activity as an extra-credit task; 1408 students responded
key_sources: Amogh Sirnoorkar and Omkar Mamidpalliwar. (2026). Students' Epistemological Beliefs and their Chatbot Preferences in AI-mediated Physics Learning. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29385

article_title: Inferring Students’ Personality from Their Communication Behavior in Web-based Learning Systems
citation: Wen Wu, Li Chen, Qingchang Yang, You Li. (2019). Inferring Students' Personality from Their Communication Behavior in Web-based Learning Systems. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-018-00173-9
title: eBanshu web-based learning system with synchronous and asynchronous communication tools
description: eBanshu is a web-based learning system released in 2013 and used by more than 20 universities in China with over 33,000 students enrolled on 100 courses. It equips online classes with synchronous tools — a text chat room, a hands-up facility for asking instructors questions, and note-taking and note-sharing facilities — and asynchronous tools including a discussion forum, a materials-sharing facility, and an assignment submission facility. In this study the communication tools were "provided for students to freely use, not counted in their final assessment", and the system automatically logged students' behavior and messages for analysis.
requirements: Instructors use video cameras and digitizers to give real-time lectures
Behavioral logs are automatically recorded for analysis
target_learners: college students in elective online courses
target_learning_goals: course learning across liberal arts, science, and engineering subjects
examples: 164 bachelor students from Hebei Normal University used eBanshu across 16 elective courses, each lasting 12 weeks with 2 lessons per week
key_sources: Wen Wu, Li Chen, Qingchang Yang, You Li. (2019). Inferring Students' Personality from Their Communication Behavior in Web-based Learning Systems. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-018-00173-9

article_title: The Measurement of Evidence-Based Healthcare Competence of Nurses and Associated Background Factors: A Scoping Review.
citation: Härkönen, H., Hannila, H.‐M., Oikarinen, A., Kääriäinen, M., Ylimäki, S., Hietaniemi, A.‐M., Holopainen, A., Jansson, M., Pölkki, T., Kaakinen, P., Kanste, O., & Tuomikoski, A.‐M. (2025). The Measurement of Evidence‐Based Healthcare Competence of Nurses and Associated Background Factors: A Scoping Review. Research in Nursing & Health, 48(5), 581–593. https://doi.org/10.1002/nur.70004
title: Evidence‐based healthcare (EBHC) competence as a measurable multidimensional construct spanning the evidence‐translation process
description: The review frames evidence‐based healthcare competence as a construct encompassing the generation, synthesis, transfer, and implementation of research evidence, with the related concept of evidence‐based practice achieved "When healthcare professionals apply the best available evidence in their decisions". Nursing competence is treated as "a complex and evolving concept that includes knowledge, skills, attitudes, beliefs, performance, and motivation", with EBP recognized as a core component. The review uses this framing to organize its mapping of 23 measurement instruments and 24 background factors, concluding that no instrument captures EBHC competence comprehensively.
requirements: Instruments must be interpreted against the multidimensional definition of EBHC competence spanning evidence generation, synthesis, transfer, and implementation
constraints: The review notes the concept of EBHC competence is complex and educational qualifications and professional roles for nurses vary between countries, which could limit how widely the results can be applied
target_learners: Nurses in direct patient care across all healthcare settings
target_learning_goals: Evidence‐based healthcare competence including knowledge, skills, attitudes, beliefs, performance, and motivation
key_sources: Härkönen, H., Hannila, H.‐M., Oikarinen, A., Kääriäinen, M., Ylimäki, S., Hietaniemi, A.‐M., Holopainen, A., Jansson, M., Pölkki, T., Kaakinen, P., Kanste, O., & Tuomikoski, A.‐M. (2025). The Measurement of Evidence‐Based Healthcare Competence of Nurses and Associated Background Factors: A Scoping Review. Research in Nursing & Health, 48(5), 581–593. https://doi.org/10.1002/nur.70004

article_title: Theory-based strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: a systematic review.
citation: Ramis Mary-Anne, Chang Anne, Conway Aaron, Lim David, Munday Judy, Nissen Lisa. (2019). Theory-based strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1698-4
title: Five theoretical frameworks underpin the theory-based undergraduate EBP interventions, but no single theory is aligned with EBP teaching and learning
description: The review identifies the theories used in the five included studies: Social Cognitive Theory (Bandura's self-efficacy construct), Rogers' Theory of Diffusion of Innovations, Cognitive Apprenticeship Theory, Cognitive Load Theory and Cognitive Flexibility Theory. CAT "posits social interactions between the learner and the expert form a base for further cognitive development", accomplished through "scaffolding, observation, modeling, mentoring, reflection and participation". The review concludes no single theory is yet aligned with EBP teaching and learning and that the most effective theory cannot be determined.
requirements: Interventions must report alignment with, and detail of, one or more theoretical frameworks to count as theory-based in this review
constraints: Due to heterogeneity in theories reported, populations and interventions it was not possible to confidently determine which theory was most effective
target_learning_goals: Evidence-based practice knowledge, skills, attitudes, behaviors and capability
examples: Kim et al. grounded their intervention in SCT self-efficacy and Rogers' Diffusion of Innovations; Ashktorab et al. mapped each intervention stage to Rogers' five stages; Long et al. linked practice opportunities to CAT's reflection component
key_sources: Ramis Mary-Anne, Chang Anne, Conway Aaron, Lim David, Munday Judy, Nissen Lisa. (2019). Theory-based strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1698-4

article_title: Theory-based strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: a systematic review.
citation: Ramis Mary-Anne, Chang Anne, Conway Aaron, Lim David, Munday Judy, Nissen Lisa. (2019). Theory-based strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1698-4
title: Evidence-based internet research tool (EBR tool) for teaching critical appraisal skills across disciplines
description: Long et al.'s intervention was an "Evidence based internet research tool for teaching students across disciplines, about EBP (particularly critical appraisal skills)". Participants viewed a 30-min training video on how to use the tool, and case-study based questions were included for students to apply question formulation and critical appraisal skills. The tool was designed to be an adjunct resource to texts and classroom education, and its use was grounded in Cognitive Apprenticeship Theory.
requirements: A 30-min training video on how to use the tool; designed as an adjunct resource to texts and classroom education
constraints: Implementation and evaluation steps of the EBP process were not specified for this intervention
target_learning_goals: EBP question formulation, searching and critical appraisal skills, credibility assessment of online sources
examples: Assessment used researcher-developed criteria based on a tool by Ivanitskaya et al., with test-retest reliability r = 0.83-0.81 for Questions 1 & 2 and 100% content validity relevance to EBP
key_sources: Ramis Mary-Anne, Chang Anne, Conway Aaron, Lim David, Munday Judy, Nissen Lisa. (2019). Theory-based strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: a systematic review. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-019-1698-4

article_title: Educational strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: systematic review.
citation: Kyriakoulis Konstantinos, Patelarou Athina, Laliotis Aggelos, Wan Andrew C, Matalliotakis Michail, Tsiou Chrysoula, Patelarou Evridiki. (2016). Educational strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: systematic review. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5066070/
title: EBP as a learnable skill framework for undergraduate health education
description: The review frames EBP as "a learnable skill", stating that "the question is not whether EBP can or should be taught, but how to best teach". This framework positions EBP competence—knowledge, skills, and attitudes—as an teachable outcome that educational interventions can improve, and organizes the review's synthesis around identifying which teaching strategies best build that competence. It treats EBP as comprising domains of research question formulation, sources of evidence, evidence appraisal, and implementation into practice.
requirements: Curriculum time and instructional strategies dedicated to EBP teaching
Assessment instruments capable of measuring EBP competence change
constraints: The review notes increase in EBP competency is dependent on a variety of factors including prior training, exposure to epidemiology, research design, biostatistics, and organizational culture and support toward EBP, none of which were adjusted for in included studies
target_learners: Undergraduate health students across medical, nursing, pharmacy, physiotherapy, and dentistry disciplines
target_learning_goals: EBP competence: knowledge, skills, and attitudes for clinical decision-making incorporating research evidence
examples: The review's 20 included studies all evaluated educational interventions designed to increase EBP competence, supporting the premise that EBP is teachable
key_sources: Kyriakoulis Konstantinos, Patelarou Athina, Laliotis Aggelos, Wan Andrew C, Matalliotakis Michail, Tsiou Chrysoula, Patelarou Evridiki. (2016). Educational strategies for teaching evidence-based practice to undergraduate health students: systematic review. Journal of Educational Evaluation for Health Professions. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5066070/

article_title: The Critical Thinking Abilities in Learning Using Elementary Algebra E-Books: A Case Study at Public Universities in Indonesia
citation: Mursalin. (2019). The Critical Thinking Abilities in Learning Using Elementary Algebra E-Books: A Case Study at Public Universities in Indonesia. Malikussaleh Journal of Mathematics Learning (MJML), 2(1), 29-33. https://doi.org/10.29103/mjml.v2i1.2292
title: Use freely available e-books as learning resources so students can study mathematics independently
description: The article recommends e-books as learning resources that "can make it easier for students to learn and understand the material independently, especially in learning mathematics", because students can read them on laptops, computers, or mobile devices wherever and whenever. In the study, e-book use in small groups guided students through analyzing problems and was associated with higher critical thinking gains. The authors frame e-book adoption as a transformation building "a new tradition for learning resources that are more dynamic, independent and inexpensive".
requirements: Adequate internet access and digital devices for students; e-books available in digital libraries
constraints: The article notes critics observe that reading on screen is an unpleasant experience that may inhibit e-book growth, and one cited study found reading e-books is not equivalent to reading textbooks
target_learners: higher education students, particularly mathematics education undergraduates
target_learning_goals: independent understanding of mathematics material and mathematical critical thinking
examples: Class A1 learned Elementary Algebra with the e-book, including small-group problem analysis and assignments delivered through the e-book
key_sources: Mursalin. (2019). The Critical Thinking Abilities in Learning Using Elementary Algebra E-Books: A Case Study at Public Universities in Indonesia. Malikussaleh Journal of Mathematics Learning (MJML), 2(1), 29-33. https://doi.org/10.29103/mjml.v2i1.2292

article_title: Improving 7th Grade Students' Epistemological Beliefs by Epistemologically Enriched Argumentation Model
citation: Kızkapan, O., & Bektaş, O. (2021). Improving 7th Grade Students’ Epistemological Beliefs by Epistemologically Enriched Argumentation Model. Pedagogical Research, 6(3), em0095. https://doi.org/10.29333/pr/10949
title: Epistemological Belief Scale (EBS) developed for the study
description: The researchers developed a Likert-type epistemological belief scale from a literature review, piloted on 700 secondary students, then refined by exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis. The final scale "consisted of four-factors": simple knowledge (11 items), justification of knowledge (9 items), innate ability (5 items) and development of knowledge (4 items), i.e., 29 items. Cronbach's alpha was .846 for SK, .812 for JK, .610 for IA and .616 for DK; CFA fit indices (RMSEA .047, CFI .96) validated the model.
requirements: Used as the quantitative pretest-posttest measure of epistemological beliefs in the group comparison
constraints: Innate ability and development of knowledge subscales show lower reliability (.610 and .616)
target_learning_goals: Measuring epistemological beliefs about scientific knowledge
examples: Sample item for justification of knowledge: Experimentation is a good way to see if something is right
key_sources: Kızkapan, O., & Bektaş, O. (2021). Improving 7th Grade Students’ Epistemological Beliefs by Epistemologically Enriched Argumentation Model. Pedagogical Research, 6(3), em0095. https://doi.org/10.29333/pr/10949

article_title: The Impact of Animated Books on the Vocabulary and Language Development of Preschool-Aged Children in Two School Settings
citation: Amy D. Broemmel, Mary Jane Moran, and Deborah A. Wooten. (2010). The Impact of Animated Books on the Vocabulary and Language Development of Preschool-Aged Children in Two School Settings. University of Tennessee. http://www.movingpicturebooks.com/downloads/the-alphabet-songbook.php
title: Animated e-books can serve as an appropriate substitute for an interactive read aloud for reinforcing preschool vocabulary learning
description: The article proposes that because children's vocabulary growth occurred with both e-books and traditional books, an e-book could replace an interactive read aloud for vocabulary reinforcement. The authors write that "an e-book could be an appropriate substitute for an interactive read aloud, thus providing teachers with more time to attend to other instructional needs that cannot be addressed by digital technology." This rests on a small pilot with no significant difference between conditions.
requirements: Multiple exposures to the book across days (children read each book at least three times per week in the study)
constraints: Findings cannot be generalized to other settings given the three-week duration and small sample; direct comparisons of classrooms are confounded by variation in teachers
examples: Experimental classrooms gave children access to two digital copies of each e-book during designated center time alongside traditional picture books in a browsing basket
key_sources: Amy D. Broemmel, Mary Jane Moran, and Deborah A. Wooten. (2010). The Impact of Animated Books on the Vocabulary and Language Development of Preschool-Aged Children in Two School Settings. University of Tennessee. http://www.movingpicturebooks.com/downloads/the-alphabet-songbook.php

article_title: Are e-Books Effective Tools for Learning? Reading Speed and Comprehension: iPad®[superscript i] vs. Paper
citation: Sackstein S, Spark L & Jenkins A. (2015). Are e-books effective tools for learning? Reading speed and comprehension: iPad vs. paper. South African Journal of Education, 35(4), Art. #1202. https://doi.org/10.15700/saje.v35n4a1202
title: Introduce e-books in classrooms without concern for hindered reading performance
description: The study concludes that e-books can be introduced in educational settings without concern that reading speed or comprehension will be hindered, based on evidence that students read at least as fast and comprehend as well on iPad as on paper. The authors state that for educators, e-books can be introduced without concern that reading performance and comprehension will be hindered. This is particularly relevant for emerging economies where lower-cost e-textbooks could replace paper textbooks.
requirements: Educators should still assess whether each individual student comprehends effectively from an electronic medium
constraints: Findings based on static electronic text only, not interactive e-books
Culturally similar and privileged sample may limit generalisability
examples: Students read from iPad and paper on different days with counterbalanced order across three experimental groups
key_sources: Sackstein S, Spark L & Jenkins A. (2015). Are e-books effective tools for learning? Reading speed and comprehension: iPad vs. paper. South African Journal of Education, 35(4), Art. #1202. https://doi.org/10.15700/saje.v35n4a1202

article_title: Knowledge, practice, and facilitating factors of evidence-based medicine among Malaysian doctors: a cross-sectional study.
citation: Albart Stephenie Ann, Looi Irene. (2025). Knowledge, practice, and facilitating factors of evidence-based medicine among Malaysian doctors: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06865-w
title: Evidence-Based Medicine Questionnaire (EBMQ)
description: The EBMQ is a validated 42-item questionnaire with Likert scales assessing doctors' knowledge, practice, and facilitating factors or barriers to implementing evidence-based medicine. It has three main domains — knowledge (24 items), practice (8 items), and facilitating factors (10 items) — scored on 4-point and 5-point Likert scales, with raw scores converted to percentages and categorised using Bloom's cutoffs. This study used Malaysia's validated version with permission, renaming the barrier domain "facilitating factors" because higher scores mean better conditions for implementing EBM.
requirements: Permission from the copyright holders to use the questionnaire without modification of the validated items
constraints: The facilitating factors and barriers evaluated were restricted to those in the EBMQ and may not cover all barriers Malaysian doctors face
It provides subjective, self-reported assessments and does not objectively assess actual EBM competencies and skills
target_learning_goals: Evidence-based medicine knowledge, practice, and implementation conditions
examples: Used as the sole instrument in a nationwide online survey of 409 Malaysian doctors conducted June to November 2022
key_sources: Albart Stephenie Ann, Looi Irene. (2025). Knowledge, practice, and facilitating factors of evidence-based medicine among Malaysian doctors: a cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06865-w

article_title: Comparison of the adequacies of the OSCE and vOSCE to assess the competencies required under Brazilian medical curriculum guidelines: a multicenter study.
citation: Sampaio Carvalho H, Barros Melo M do C, Kakehasi FM, Menezes Ferri Liu P, Gontijo Minafra Silveira Santos F, de Melo Martins RL, Vale de Castro Monteiro M, Chaves Campos ME, Esteves RZ, Belloni Torsani M, Lopes Calvo T I de F, Inca Atahualpa Urdiales A, De Marco Novellino AM, Viana Zuza DR, Ferreira Moura H, de Vilhena Toledo MA, Machado Saldanha CR, Pedrosa Ribeiro Alves Oliveira A, Zen Tempski P, de Souza Santos I, de Arruda Martins M. (2025). Comparison of the adequacies of the OSCE and vOSCE to assess the competencies required under Brazilian medical curriculum guidelines: a multicenter study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06631-4
title: The EBSERH vOSCE: a validated virtual competency-assessment model with simulated patients, multiple response formats, and system feedback
description: The article describes a virtual OSCE model developed by the Brazilian Hospital Services Company (EBSERH), a federal institution managing 51 federal teaching hospitals. "The model developed by EBSERH contains case scenarios in a primary, secondary or tertiary health care clinical setting," and "Students can express their competences through open written text, structured objective responses, voice responses, video capture or a combination of these." Interaction occurs with simulated patients or avatars; students explain diagnoses and prognosis on video at the end of each case; and the grade is assigned by a professional not involved in implementation. The model was "applied to a group of 300 final-year medical students from several universities for validation," with each student completing 5 cases of 10 to 15 min.
requirements: Requires a database of histories and physical exams for each type of case, trained evaluators uninvolved with implementation, and response formats suited to each question
constraints: The study analyzed only example videos of the model; data concerning student performance or technical content of the videos were not analyzed
target_learning_goals: clinical competencies of knowledge, skills and attitudes (history taking, physical signs, medical decision-making, diagnosis, patient communication)
examples: The model's videos, produced from vOSCEs taken by 300 final-year medical students, were used as training examples for medical residency preceptors
key_sources: Sampaio Carvalho H, Barros Melo M do C, Kakehasi FM, Menezes Ferri Liu P, Gontijo Minafra Silveira Santos F, de Melo Martins RL, Vale de Castro Monteiro M, Chaves Campos ME, Esteves RZ, Belloni Torsani M, Lopes Calvo T I de F, Inca Atahualpa Urdiales A, De Marco Novellino AM, Viana Zuza DR, Ferreira Moura H, de Vilhena Toledo MA, Machado Saldanha CR, Pedrosa Ribeiro Alves Oliveira A, Zen Tempski P, de Souza Santos I, de Arruda Martins M. (2025). Comparison of the adequacies of the OSCE and vOSCE to assess the competencies required under Brazilian medical curriculum guidelines: a multicenter study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06631-4
